plain_text:
Between 2010 and 2024, climate action in the AFOLU and the waste sectors saw only limited progress
Figure 3.4). Both sectors – covered for the first time by the CAPMF (Box 3.1) – lagged behind
energy-related sectors such as electricity, transport, buildings and industry. This reflects challenges
associated with mitigation in these areas despite agriculture’s high vulnerability to climate change
(Chapter 1). With emissions from agriculture and waste still rising in many countries (Chapter 2), stronger
efforts are needed to reverse the trend. Encouragingly, some countries have begun to act in these sectors:
for example, Australia and Germany included waste in their ETSs, and Denmark introduced a pricing
mechanism for GHG emissions from agriculture (Box 3.3).
semantic_text: Between 2010 and 2024, climate action in the AFOLU and the waste sectors saw only limited progress Figure 3.4). Both sectors – covered for the first time by the CAPMF (Box 3.1) – lagged behind energy-related sectors such as electricity, transport, buildings and industry. This reflects challenges associated with mitigation in these areas despite agriculture’s high vulnerability to climate change (Chapter 1). With emissions from agriculture and waste still rising in many countries (Chapter 2), stronger efforts are needed to reverse the trend. Encouragingly, some countries have begun to act in these sectors: for example, Australia and Germany included waste in their ETSs, and Denmark introduced a pricing mechanism for GHG emissions from agriculture (Box 3.3).
